Idumea
ĭd-ū-mē´ȧ
n. (the Greek name for Edom; the land of Esau's descendants, standing under a particular judgment)
Greek Idoumaia, from Hebrew Edom, red — the name Esau earned over a bowl of red pottage. The nation and the birthright sale carry the same word.

Biblical Definition

Isaiah makes Idumea the type of the nations under the sword: “my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment” (Isa 34:5), “for the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea” (Isa 34:6), and gives the reason: “it is the day of the LORD'S vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion” (Isa 34:8). Ezekiel names the specific offence: “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee” (Eze 35:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines vengeance as the infliction of pain on another in return for an injury or offense, and when used of God, the just retribution of punishment.

expand to see more

VENGEANCE, n. The infliction of pain on another, in return for an injury or offense. Such infliction, when it proceeds from malice, is revenge, and morally wrong; when the infliction proceeds from justice, it is vengeance, and lawful.

RECOMPENSE, n. An equivalent returned for any thing given, done or suffered; compensation; reward; requital.

CONTROVERSY, n. Dispute; debate; agitation of contrary opinions; also, in Scripture, a cause pleaded.

Key Scripture

Isa 34:5 — "For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment."

Isa 34:8 — "For it is the day of the LORD'S vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion."

Eze 35:15 — "As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it: and they shall know that I am the LORD."

Oba 1:10 — "For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever."

Modern Corruption

Edom is judged for standing on the other side in the day of his brother's calamity, and Obadiah names the sin as violence against a brother.

expand to see more

Obadiah is one chapter long and it is entirely about this. Edom did not sack Jerusalem; Edom watched. Thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces; thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Ezekiel says the same — as thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee. The gladness of a bystander is charged as violence against a brother.

The corruption to name is the conviction that spectatorship is innocent. Edom's hands did not open the gate, and Edom is cut off for ever. Proverbs 24:17-18 legislates for the same heart in private life: rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth, lest the LORD see it, and it displease him. Behind the whole account lies a birthright sold for one morsel of meat, of which Hebrews 12:16 warns the church directly. Idumea in the prophets is not merely a neighbouring state; it is what a man's descendants become when he despises what God gave him and hates the brother who received it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Edom (H123), red, Edom; Seir (H8165), the mountain of Edom; naqam (H5359), vengeance; rib (H7379), controversy, cause.

expand to see more

Hebrew Edom (H123) — Edom, Idumea; Isaiah 34:5, Genesis 25:30, Obadiah 1:1.

Hebrew Seir (H8165) — Mount Seir; Ezekiel 35:15, Genesis 36:8.

Hebrew naqam (H5359) — vengeance; Isaiah 34:8, Deuteronomy 32:35.

Hebrew rib (H7379) — controversy, cause, suit; Isaiah 34:8, Micah 6:2.

Hebrew chamas (H2555) — violence, wrong; Obadiah 1:10, Genesis 6:11.

Usage

"“It shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse” — Isaiah's sword."

"“As thou didst rejoice… so will I do unto thee” — the sentence fits the sin."

"“For thy violence against thy brother Jacob” — Obadiah's charge."
